method: Read305 additional keyboard/character-handler lines. Tested non-unwinding ABI mechanism in isolated synthetic subprocess, not upstream application.
findings: Synthetic rustc panic=unwind child used same essential pattern: catch_unwind closure calls extern system function that panics. Child terminated by signal6 with non-unwinding panic message, never reaching caught-result print. Confirms mechanism on current macOS host; Windows application crash not reproduced. Prior catch wrapper cannot be credited as verified recovery.

Original wnd_proc catches closure calling wnd_proc_inner, which is itself extern system. This source structure crosses a non-unwinding boundary inside the catch; changing local research code is not changing upstream production.

Chat input edits move/delete at UTF8 char boundaries. This is Unicode scalar handling, not full grapheme editing; combining sequences may be removed separately. wm_char_decode implementation remains unread, so surrogate correctness not yet qualified.
Note editor appends characters and backspace pops final scalar; arrow keys scroll rather than moving an editing cursor. Save/close implementation remains unread; no note persistence claim.

ai_pending keyboard branch does not universally return after non-Escape keys. When chat_input_active/answer also set, Enter can reach follow-up dispatch in this read branch. start_follow_up_chat may guard pending internally and remains unread; overlapping request reachability still not proven.

Control-C in answer panel copies entire stored answer; input selection flag shared across chat/query handling. Correct focus transitions and cursor state need whole-callgraph or UI fixtures, not inferred from individual insertion branches.
limits: 85/268 whole files; main.rs partial ranges only.
ABI fixture verifies mechanism on macOS, not actual Windows callback, malformed settings or upstream suite.
No production edits.155/500 full repositories unchanged; pHash/ASAN deferred.
